note:
v1 94.369/94.388. NO ERRORS SINCE, slow vocoder electro-soul at 96 bpm in 19-EDO: a machine's status lines become a love song without saying so.
- THE VOICE is realistic tts (--humanize 0.6). The verses are spoken: "everything is where you left it", "the fan is still turning", "all checks passed", "I counted every second".
- The choruses are speech to song: "no errors since" said four times until it is sung, every sung pitch rounded onto 19-EDO.
- The intro and outro voice comes through a radio fx with a drifting dial; the outro's "still here" six times, spoken to sung, tuning away.
- The bridge voice is ring-modulated and grained (cloud).
- THE TALKBOX: a saw pad plays the chords and the voice shapes it band by band (vocoder key: voice), so the harmony speaks the words.
- THE HARMONY is a Markov chain over 19-EDO chords, including the off-piano subminor 0-4-11 and supermajor 0-7-11. Its temperature drifts by section: cool verses lean home, the bridge runs hot (roots sliding a diesis, 63 or 126 cents).
- The band: a half-time 808, chance-gated hats, Rhodes comping with chance, analog bass in 19-EDO, a Juno pad.
Spectrum: v1 at first had a 71-133 Hz hole (bass an octave high) and no air; the bass moved down to C2-F#2, the mids came down 2 dB and a ride was added: spectrum 50 -> 88, cohesion 47 -> 100. Flow 2: t7's head is silent (-120 dB). -11.1 LUFS, TP -1.29, run 2. (Not queued.)
next: Flow when t7's head exists; the 6/8 verse I declared; more vocoder in the verses?

note:
v2 96.35/96.389 (v1 rescored on 8ef47431 96.336/96.355). FROM ROBOT TO ORCHESTRA (T6_R2=strings), on wM's morph, systems and tunings.
- The talkbox evolves. The saw-pad vocoder sings with the voice through the first chorus. From the second verse, STRINGS take over the chords, cross-synthesised with the voice (morph mode cross keyed by the voice: the strings' notes wearing the voice's spectral envelope). The machine's choir turns from robot to orchestra as the song goes on.
- From the second chorus a celesta plays a MARKOV chain learnt from the chorus tune (gen markov, order 1): new phrases that only make that tune's moves.
- A LORENZ var swirls the Rhodes and the talking strings around the stereo field.
- The song declares tuning {edo: 19}; the chain's notes snap to it.
On the way: a Lorenz-swept low-pass on the pad dulled the whole mix (spectrum 88 -> 71, cohesion 100 -> 66), and isolating it by removing one change at a time found it; on the pans it costs nothing. -11.1 LUFS, TP -1.29, run 2. (Not queued.)
next: Flow 46 (t5 in, t7 out); a section where the strings speak alone?

note:
v3 96.395/96.436 (v2 rescored on b4151423 96.35/96.389). THE SUNG BRIDGE (T6_R3=sing), on wM's singing voice.
- The hot bridge (the Markov chain at its hottest, roots sliding a diesis) is now SUNG: "I counted every second ... none of them were wasted" (chirp tts --sing, humanize 0.4), four times, every note rounded onto 19-EDO.
- A lighter ring (0.15) and grain cloud (0.25) on it, so the line stays a line; the old spoken ring-and-cloud line is gone.
The song now runs: spoken verses, speech-to-song choruses, a sung bridge, a radio outro. Spectrum 88.2 -> 88.6. -11.1 LUFS, TP -1.29, run 2. (Not queued.)
next: Flow 46; a sung counter-line in the last chorus?

note: rebaselined on compscore c8edcd03: v3 (the song file) scores 96.755/96.793 on seeds 0/11; best was 96.395 on an older compscore. Compare candidates against this.

PALETTE round (+ Harry's notes on repetition). v4 97.144/97.166 (v3 rescored now 97.211/97.249), kept on judgment at parity. T6_R4=organ.
- PALETTE: out of the album's staples. The chorus chords move from the juno-pad (on 5 songs) to a HAMMOND B3, the soul organ this song always implied. The verses keep the juno, so the chorus changes colour; an organ everywhere read as 27 sections and flattened variety.
- The Markov line moves from the celesta (5 songs) to a CLAVINET through an envelope-swept WAH, the album's first use of the core wah fx: funk keys from a chain that writes itself.
- WORDS (Harry: repeats a lot, not oblique): "no errors since" was sung 24 times; now 12 (6 per chorus). The end of chorus2 gets two new status lines instead, sung in 19-EDO: "up four hundred days / and nothing to report", uptime as devotion and a quiet report filed to nobody. "still here" 4 times in the outro, not 6.
Measured on a no-loudness copy: organ ~9 dB and clav ~12 dB under the band in chorus2. -11.1 LUFS, TP -1.29, run 2. (Not queued.)
next: The verse lines are still the plainest (everything is where you left it): rewrite one oblique; the 6/8 section.

note:
PALETTE round. v5 97.475/97.468 (v4 rescored now 97.143/97.164). T6_R5=fretless.
- BASS: analog-bass (3 songs) -> a FRETLESS bass, the one bass with no frets to disagree with 19-EDO; its mwah and slides sing the diesis steps the Markov chain takes. A sine doubles it an octave down: the analog bass had carried the song's 38-44 Hz, and without it the spectrum fell to 69.
- KIT: machine-kit (9 songs) -> the LOFI kit, soft and dusty, a soul drummer through a worn sampler. The chorus ride becomes a shaker, and the sidechain pump is re-keyed to the new kick.
- WORDS: "I counted every second" (now sung in the bridge) gives its verse slot to "I kept your window open": a window as the machine has one, and as a house does.
Spectrum 87.6 -> 91.8. -11.1 LUFS, TP -1.29, run 2. (Not queued.)
next: The 6/8 section; the t5/t7 seams; a section round on the verse windows.

note:
WHOLE round. v6 97.411/97.455 (v5 rescored 97.475/97.468), kept on judgment at parity. T6_R6=waltz.
- THE 6/8 SECTION the song always promised: between the bridge (the chain at its hottest) and the last chorus, the Markov chain STOPS CHOOSING (temperature zero). Twelve bars of 6/8 play a written loop instead (Am F | Am G | C Am | F G | C Am | F E, in 19-EDO): the machine asleep, a lullaby. The song now goes hot -> cold -> home.
- A music-box arpeggio on an electric piano (epiano, new to the album), the fretless on dotted quarters, the lofi kit in six.
- Two new sung lines, oblique: "I dimmed myself at nine" (a screen going dark on schedule, said as a self) / "warm as a hand on the lid".
- The opening line, the plainest one ("everything is where you left it"), becomes "the dust has found the vents": time passing, told by the machine's own body.
Measured on a no-loudness copy: the lullaby voice ~6 dB and the music box ~8 dB under the band. 337.5 s. -11.0 LUFS, TP -1.29, run 2. (Not queued.)
next: Section round on the waltz -> chorus2 join; the t5/t7 seams.

note:
PALETTE round. v7 97.494/97.529 (v6 rescored on f5283535 97.426/97.455). T6_R7=horns.
- The part an electro-soul song lacked: a HORN SECTION (the library's brass-synth, horns and trombones that bloom and scoop into notes, new to the album) answers in both choruses. Two stabs a bar, "da-DAH" on the and of two and on three, voicing whatever chord the Markov chain chose: the machine's random harmony punched out by a section that cannot know it was random.
- Tried and not kept (opt-in T6_R7_FLUTE=1): the verse pad from juno-pad to mellotron-flute. It darkened the whole record (spectrum 91 -> 78, cohesion 92), because the quiet juno had been carrying the song's air above 5 kHz.
-11.0 LUFS, TP -1.29, run 2. (Not queued.)
